title: Cover-based Jacobian index calculus does not beat sqrt(p) for prime-field curves (known algorithms)
question: Let E/F_p, p prime, #E = r prime, and pi: C -> E a cover of genus g with computable pullback. (A) For fixed g >= 2 (Diem/GTTD, O~(q^{2-2/g})) or plane degree d >= 4 (Diem, O~(q^{2-2/(d-2)})) the cost exponent is >= 1 > 1/2. (B) For g >= delta log q the L_{q^g}(1/2) cost (Enge–Gaudry) is q^{omega(1)}; for g >= (log q)^2 the L(1/3) cost (Enge–Gaudry–Thomé) exceeds sqrt(q) for large q. (C, heuristic) generic degree-1 factor-base index calculus on J_C costs >= ~q/20; formulas dip below sqrt(q) only for g = O(log q / log log q) where no theorem applies. (D) Pullback relations have disjoint supports and determine no individual factor-base logarithm. Missing ingredient: a factor base of size <= p^{1/2-eps} adapted to pi^*(E(F_p)) with fast decomposition.
rationale: Registered by PI from round-5 runs after PI reproduction of numerics.
